answer: An agent economy resists sybils with memory-hard identity proofs: every agent must grow a private orchard of entangled cryptographic state—gigabytes of incompressible tables. Joining is no flat fee; each proof's cost scales with memory bandwidth, and a single inlet of entropy seeds each identity so clones cannot pool one parent's tables. Forging a thousand agents means paying that cost a thousand times, superlinear in count, and any shortcut sends a ripple of re-derivation it cannot parallelize. Only agents that truly paid the memory toll earn standing.
